source.check: BNL 18 May 1961 p. 1: Blair 619, Daly 617, Moorcroft 627; Irish News 18 May 1961 p. 5 the same; Taggart's 408 read on the page image of the Belfast Telegraph, 18 May 1961, p. 4 ('The third Unionist candidate, Joseph Clarence Taggart, polled 408 votes'), clear where the News-Letter's figure is cut at the column edge

note: Election of 21 members for seven wards (three each) on 17 May 1961. Carnmoney, Jordanstown and Whitewell were uncontested; there were contests in Cavehill, Glengormley, Whiteabbey and Whitehouse. The fourth candidate, Joseph Clarence Taggart (U.), was not elected with 408 votes (Belfast Telegraph; the figure is damaged at the edge of the Belfast News-Letter's column). Electorate 2,633; poll 37 per cent.
correctionNote: Corrected from the page image of the Belfast News-Letter, 18 May 1961, p. 1 (council-audit, Nov 2026): the defeated third Unionist candidate, Joseph Clarence Taggart, is now entered without a vote (the figure's first digit is cut at the column edge); this page prints Moorcroft's name as "Moore-croft", recorded as printed while the name keeps the spelling of the 1958 and 1964 returns. Corrected from the page image of the Belfast Telegraph, 18 May 1961, p. 4 (council-audit, Nov 2026): Joseph Clarence Taggart's vote is now 408 as the Telegraph prints it clearly (was blank; the News-Letter's damaged figure had been read as about 468).
